problems.problem: A triangle has area $1$ and side lengths $a\ge b\ge c$. Prove that $b\ge\sqrt2$.
An arithmetic progression consists of integers. One of its terms is the fifth power of an integer. Prove that infinitely many terms have this property.

The legislature of a country has $r$ members and works through $N$ committees. Every committee has exactly nine members, every legislator belongs to exactly $n$ committees, and every three legislators belong together to exactly one committee. (a) Express $N$ and $n$ in terms of $r$. (b) Prove that $r$ is divisible by neither $7$ nor $4$.
Find all positive integers $n$ for which $2^n+2^8+2^{11}$ is a perfect square.

A hunter is lost in a simply connected open forest of area $S$. He does not know the shape of the forest, but knows its area. He has no compass. Prove that he can leave the forest after walking a distance no greater than $2\sqrt{\pi S}$. Assume that he can follow a route that he plans.
Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral. Points $M$ and $P$ are the midpoints of $BC$ and $CD$, respectively, and $AM+AP=a$. Prove that the area of $ABCD$ is less than $a^2/2$.
Find real values of $a,b$ for which the equation $$\sqrt[3]{(ax+b)^2}+\sqrt[3]{(ax-b)^2}+\sqrt[3]{a^2x^2-b^2}=\sqrt[3]b$$ has exactly one real solution.
Evaluate $\sec^2(\pi/9)+\sec^2(5\pi/9)+\sec^2(7\pi/9)$.

Point $R$ lies between $P$ and $Q$ on a line. Let $A,B,C_0$ be the circles with diameters $PQ,PR,RQ$, respectively. In the upper semicircle of $A$, construct a chain of distinct circles $C_1,C_2,\ldots$: $C_1$ is tangent internally to $A$ and externally to $B,C_0$, and $C_n$ is tangent internally to $A$ and externally to $B,C_{n-1}$. Let $r_n$ be the radius of $C_n$ and $Y_n$ the distance from its centre to the line $PR$. Prove that $Y_n=2nr_n$.

Prove that $6^x=y^2+y-2$ has no solutions in integers $x,y$.

Let $m,n$ be positive integers, let $c$ be a positive irrational number, and put $d=1/c$. Prove that $$\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor m+nc\rfloor}\left\lfloor(n+1)+(m-j)d\right\rfloor=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor n+md\rfloor}\left\lfloor(m+1)+(n-j)c\right\rfloor.$$ Here $\lfloor x\rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $x$.

Points $X,A,B,C,D$ lie on a line $\ell$. Let $H$ be a point outside $\ell$, and let $K$ be another point on $XH$. Lines $HA,KB$ meet at $P$, and lines $HC,KD$ meet at $Q$. Let $Y=PQ\cap\ell$. Assuming these intersections are defined, prove that the position of $Y$ depends only on $X,A,B,C,D$, and not on $H,K$.
Prove that, for every integer $n>1$, the nested radical $$\sqrt{1+\sqrt{2+\sqrt{3+\cdots+\sqrt n}}}$$ is irrational.
Real angles $x,y,z$ satisfy $x+y+z=2\pi$ and $\cos x\cos y\cos z=1/4$. Prove that $$4\cos(3x)\cos(3y)\cos(3z)-12\cos(2x)\cos(2y)\cos(2z)=1.$$
For which nonzero real values of $a$ does $$a^2\left|a+\frac{x}{a^2}\right|+|1+x|=1-a^3$$ have more than three integer solutions $x$?

In tetrahedron $MABC$, the edges $MA,MB,MC$ are pairwise perpendicular. The areas of faces $MAB,MAC,MBC$ are $S_1,S_2,S_3$, respectively, and the altitude from $M$ to $ABC$ has length $h$. Prove that $S_1+S_2+S_3\ge9h^2/2$.
Find a positive integer $k$ such that every solution $x$, measured in degrees, of $$(2\sqrt2\cos25^\circ-1)\tan(x^\circ)=(2\sqrt2\sin25^\circ-1)\tan((kx)^\circ)$$ is an integer.
For a positive integer $n$, let $\sigma(n)$ be the sum of its positive divisors. Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which $\sigma(n!)>3n!$.

Let $A$ be a set of $21$ distinct positive integers not exceeding $64$. Let $B=\{a_j-a_i:1\le i<j\le21\}$, where $a_1<\cdots<a_{21}$ are the elements of $A$. Prove that at least one of $5,6,11$ belongs to $B$.

A chord $AB$ divides a circle $M$ into arcs $p,q$. Let $O$ be the point of $q$ farthest from $AB$. A circle $\mu$ lies inside $M$ and is tangent internally to the arc $p$ and to the line $AB$. Prove that the length of a tangent segment from $O$ to $\mu$ equals $OA$.

Positive real numbers $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ and $q_1,\ldots,q_n$ satisfy $\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=\sum_{i=1}^n q_i$. Prove that $$\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\ln p_i\ge\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\ln q_i.$$
Solve $\lfloor4x-1/5\rfloor-3x+4=0$ over the real numbers, where $\lfloor t\rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $t$.

Let $f(n)$ be the number of trailing zeros in the decimal representation of $n!$. (a) Prove that $f(5745)-f(1985)=f(5745-1985)$. (b) Is $f(x)-f(y)=f(x-y)$ true for every pair of positive integers $x>y$? Justify your answer.
Find all real values of $a$ for which $$ (\sin x)^{\sqrt{3x-1}}+2(\cos2x)^{\sqrt{-9x^2-3x+2}}-\log_{1/x}(x^3)=a$$ has at least one real solution.

On the $64$ squares of a chessboard stand $32$ white pieces and $32$ black pieces. A pair of pieces is called regular if its pieces have different colours and lie in the same row or the same column; a piece may belong to several regular pairs. Let $N$ be the number of regular pairs. Prove that $N\le256$. Can equality occur? If so, determine the conditions for equality; if not, prove that it cannot.
A triangle $M$ is called special if there is a triangle $N$ similar but not congruent to $M$, and two side lengths of $N$ equal two side lengths of $M$. Characterise all special triangles.
Let $A<B$ be positive integers. Prove that among any $B$ consecutive positive integers there are two whose product is divisible by $AB$.
If $a,b,c$ are the side lengths of a triangle, prove that $$\frac32\le\frac{a}{b+c}+\frac{b}{c+a}+\frac{c}{a+b}<2.$$
Positive integers $N,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfy $N\ge a_1>a_2>\cdots>a_n\ge1$. Suppose that the least common multiple of every pair $a_i,a_j$ is at most $N$. Prove that $a_i\le N/i$ for every $i$.
For every positive integer $m$ and real $\alpha$, prove that $$x^{m+1}\cos((m-1)\alpha)-x^m\cos(m\alpha)-x\cos\alpha+1$$ is divisible by $x^2-2x\cos\alpha+1$.
Find all integer pairs $(x,y)$ satisfying $(x-1)x(x+1)=y^5$.
Prove that there are no integers $x,y$ satisfying $x^3-y^3=5746$.
A semicircle has diameter $AB$. Among all convex $n$-gons whose vertices lie in this semicircle, which has the greatest area? Justify your answer.
An infinite sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ consists of pairwise distinct real numbers. Prove that it has an infinite monotone subsequence.
Let $a<b<c$ be real numbers and let $p,q,r$ be positive real numbers. Prove that $$\frac{p}{x-a}+\frac{q}{x-b}+\frac{r}{x-c}=1$$ has three real solutions, exactly one of which is greater than $c$.

Let $ABCD A'B'C'D'$ be a parallelepiped. A plane through $C'$ lies outside the interior of the parallelepiped and meets the rays $AB,AD,AA'$ at $P,Q,R$, respectively. Determine the positions of $P,Q,R$ that minimise the volume of the pyramid $APQR$.

For integers $i\ge0$ and $j\in\mathbb Z$, define $a_{i,j}$ by $a_{0,0}=1$, $a_{0,j}=0$ for $j\ne0$, and $$a_{i,j}=2(a_{i-1,j-1}+a_{i-1,j+1})-a_{i-1,j}\qquad(i>0).$$ Prove that $$a_{n,0}=(-1)^n\sum_{r=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}2^{2r}\frac{n!}{(n-2r)!(r!)^2}.$$

List all $n!$ permutations $\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_{n!}$ of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. If $\pi_k=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$, put $S_k=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(a_i-a_{i+1})^2$. Evaluate the arithmetic mean $\frac1{n!}\sum_{k=1}^{n!}S_k$.
Prove that there is no positive decimal integer such that moving its first digit from the left to the right end produces four times the original integer.

Find all pairs $(\alpha,x)$, where $\alpha$ is an integer and $x$ is real, satisfying $$\left\lfloor\frac{\alpha^2x+\alpha^2-1}{2}\right\rfloor=\frac{2x+3}{5}.$$ Here $\lfloor t\rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $t$.
Find all pairs of nonzero integers $(x,y)$ satisfying $(x^2+y)(x+y^2)=(x-y)^3$.

A triangle $ABC$ rotates in its plane about $A$, giving a triangle $AB'C'$. When the lines $BB'$ and $CC'$ meet, call their intersection $M$. (a) Find the locus of $M$. (b) Locate $M$ on this locus after a rotation through $90^\circ$.
Compare the coefficients of $x^{5748}$ in $(1-x^{19}+x^{88})^{1988}$ and $(1-x^{19}-x^{88})^{1988}$. Which is greater? Justify your answer.
Let $n$ be a positive integer and $x=\pi/(2(n+1))$. Prove that $$\sum_{j=2}^n\sec(jx)\sec((j-2)x)=3\cos(2x)\csc^2(2x).$$

Let $ABCD A'B'C'D'$ be a cube. Point $M$ lies on the diagonal $A'D$ of face $ADD'A'$, and point $N$ lies on the diagonal $BC'$ of face $BCC'B'$. Let $P$ be the midpoint of $MN$. Find the locus of $P$.

A group of people visits an exhibition of $200$ paintings. No visitor sees all the paintings, but every painting is seen by at least one visitor. Prove that there are visitors $A,B$ and paintings $\alpha,\beta$ such that $A$ sees $\alpha$ but not $\beta$, while $B$ sees $\beta$ but not $\alpha$.
Prove that a convex polygon cannot have more than three acute angles.
Find all possible values of $k$ such that all four roots of $x^4-10x^3+35x^2-50x+24=k$ are integers.
There are $n>1$ points in a disk of radius $R$. Prove that two of them are at a distance smaller than $2R/(\sqrt n-1)$.
Prove that there are no real numbers $x,y,z$ satisfying $\cos(y-z)+\cos(z-x)+\cos(x-y)+2=0$.
For every positive integer $n\ge3$, prove that there is a set of $n$ points in a plane, not all collinear, such that the distance between every two is an integer.
An acute triangle has a square inscribed in it. Prove that the incentre of the triangle lies inside the square.

Positive real numbers $a,b,c$ satisfy $a+b+c=\sqrt3/2$. Find all positive real triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $$\sqrt{y^2-a^2}+\sqrt{z^2-a^2}=\sqrt{z^2-b^2}+\sqrt{x^2-b^2}=\sqrt{x^2-c^2}+\sqrt{y^2-c^2}=1.$$
How many five-digit decimal integers with distinct digits have middle digit $5$ and an absolute difference of $3$ between their first and last digits?
Find all integer pairs $(x,y)$ satisfying $x(5y-7)=y^2+2$.

Let $X$ be a set of six points in a plane. Let $D$ be the greatest distance between two points of $X$ and $d$ the smallest. Prove that $D\ge\sqrt3\,d$. Can equality occur? If so, under what conditions?

Three lines $\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3$ pass through one point, and $A$ lies on $\ell_1$. Show that it is impossible to choose $B\in\ell_2$ and $C\in\ell_3$ so that the three given lines are the internal angle bisectors of triangle $ABC$.
A function $f$ is defined for all rational numbers and satisfies $f(1)=3$ and $f(a+b)+f(a-b)=2(f(a)+f(b))$ for all rational $a,b$. Find $f(x)$.
Solve the system $$\frac{3(x^2+1)}x=\frac{4(y^2+1)}y=\frac{5(z^2+1)}z,\qquad yz+xz+xy=1.$$

For plane points $X,Y$, define $F_Y(X)=Z$ by rotating the direction from $Y$ to $X$ counterclockwise through $90^\circ$, then taking $Z$ in the new direction with $YZ=XY$. Let $A,B,C,D$ be four points, and define $$P_1=F_A(P_0),\quad P_2=F_B(P_1),\quad P_3=F_C(P_2),\quad P_4=F_D(P_3).$$ Suppose $P_4=P_0$. Prove that (a) $AC\perp BD$ and $AC=BD$; (b) $P_4=P_0$ for every choice of $P_0$.
Prove that there are no positive real numbers $x,y$ satisfying $x^{19}y^{92}=2^{1992}$ and $19x+92y=5752$.
Prove that there is no polyhedron with exactly seven edges.
Consider the system $x_rx_{r+1}=r$ for $r=1,\ldots,n-1$, and $x_nx_1=n$. (a) Prove that it has no solution when $n$ is even. (b) Solve it when $n$ is odd.

A set of $10n$ points in a plane has no three collinear. Prove that one can construct $n$ hexagons and $n$ quadrilaterals using these points as vertices so that no two of the $2n$ polygons have a common point, either on their boundaries or in their interiors.
For positive real numbers $x,y,z$, prove that $\min(1,x^3,y^4,z^5)\le xyz$.
Let $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $C=(2,0)$. Find the locus of points $P$ satisfying $\angle PBC=2\angle PAC+\pi/2$: obtain its equation, determine the domain, sketch the locus and find its asymptotes.

Positive numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ form an arithmetic progression, and positive numbers $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ form a geometric progression. Suppose $a_1=b_1$ and $a_n=b_n$. Prove that $\sum_{r=1}^n a_r\ge\sum_{r=1}^n b_r$, and determine when equality holds.
Let $a>0$, $a\ne1$, and let $m$ be real. Solve $\log_{\sqrt a}\sqrt x=\log_a(m/x+1)$. Does a solution always exist? Justify your answer.
For positive real numbers $a,b,c$, prove that $$\frac{a^8+b^8+c^8}{a^3b^3c^3}\ge\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c.$$
Prove that there are no positive integers $x,y$ satisfying $x^3+y^3=5753^2$.

In triangle $ABC$, suppose $AC<AB$. Points $X\in AB$ and $Y\in BC$ satisfy $AX=BY$. The proposed conclusion is $XY>AC/2$. The published source notes that this claim, as stated, is false: give a counterexample instead of a proof.
For given $a,b>0$, solve $\sin x+\sin y=2a$, $\cos x+\cos y=2b$, with $0\le x,y\le2\pi$.
Find positive integers $n,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=1993$ and $\prod_{i=1}^n a_i$ is as large as possible.

A right prism has a square base of side $2a$ and height $a(1+\sqrt3)$. One base is inscribed in a sphere and the other is tangent to that same sphere. Find the sphere's radius and the volume of the part of the prism lying inside the sphere.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle, and let $L$ be the line through $C$ parallel to $AB$. The bisector of $\angle A$ meets $L$ at $E$ and $CB$ at $D$; the bisector of $\angle B$ meets $L$ at $G$ and $AC$ at $F$. Given that $DE=FG$, prove that the triangle is isosceles.
Let $p,q$ be positive integers. A function $f$ takes positive integers to positive integers and satisfies $f(xf(y))=x^py^q$ for all positive integers $x,y$. Prove that $q$ is a perfect square.
A polygon has $1994$ sides of lengths $a_i=\sqrt{4+i^2}$ for $i=1,\ldots,1994$. Prove that its vertices cannot all be lattice points, that is, points with integer coordinates.
Find the smallest $N$ such that every $N$-element subset of $\{1,2,\ldots,100\}$ contains an arithmetic progression of $11$ distinct terms.

Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be given real numbers not all zero, and let $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ be real numbers not all zero. Prove that the inequality $$r_1(x_1-a_1)+\cdots+r_n(x_n-a_n)\le\sqrt{x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2}-\sqrt{a_1^2+\cdots+a_n^2}$$ holds for all real $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ if and only if $r_i=\dfrac{a_i}{\sqrt{a_1^2+\cdots+a_n^2}}$ for every $i$.
Let $N>1$ be a positive integer. Prove that the decimal representation of $N^4$ contains at least four digits different from zero.

Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle C=90^\circ$. Points $P\in CA$ and $Q\in CB$ satisfy $\angle CQA=\angle CAB$ and $\angle CPB=\angle CBA$. Choose $R\in CA$ and $S\in BC$ so that $\angle ABR=\angle BAS=90^\circ-\angle ABC$. Find $$\frac{CP}{CS}+\frac{CQ}{CR}+\frac{BR}{BS}.$$
Solve the system over the real numbers: $$\begin{cases}x+\log(x+\sqrt{x^2+1})=y,\\y+\log(y+\sqrt{y^2+1})=z,\\z+\log(z+\sqrt{z^2+1})=x.\end{cases}$$

Let $H$ be a semicircle with diameter $PQ$. A circle $O$ is internally tangent to $H$ and touches the diameter $PQ$ at $C$. Points $A$ on $H$ and $B$ on $PQ$ are such that $AB$ is perpendicular to $PQ$ and tangent to $O$. Prove that $AC$ bisects $\angle PAB$.
For positive integers $k,n$, prove that $$\frac1{kn}+\frac1{kn+1}+\cdots+\frac1{(k+1)n-1}\ge n\left(\sqrt[n]{\frac{k+1}{k}}-1\right).$$
Find all integers $m,n$ satisfying $m^3-n^3-9mn=27$.

Let $n$ be an odd positive integer, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be distinct real numbers with $|x_i-x_j|\le1$ for $1\le i<j\le n$. Prove that $$\sum_{i<j}|x_i-x_j|\le\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor\left(\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor+1\right).$$

A $1995\times1995$ square board is given. A colouring of its cells is called good if the cells can be rearranged to produce a coloured square board symmetric about the main diagonal. Find all values of $k$ for which every $k$-colouring of the board is good.

There are $n$ countries with an airline connecting every pair, but some airlines have closed. Prove that if at most $n-3$ airlines have closed, one can make a round trip using the remaining airlines, starting in one country, visiting every country exactly once, and returning to the starting country.
For a given real number $\alpha$, find all functions $f:\mathbb R_{>0}\to\mathbb R_{>0}$ satisfying $$\alpha x^2f(1/x)+f(x)=\frac{x}{x+1}\qquad(x>0).$$
Let $a$ be a prime and $n>2$ a positive integer. Find all integer solutions of $x^n+ay^n=a^2z^n$.
Find all polynomials $P$ such that $P(x+1)-2P(x)-P(x-1)=x$ for every $x$.

Triangle $ABC$ has side lengths $a,b,c$ opposite angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$. Let $AD$ be the altitude to $BC$, $CF$ the median from $C$, and $BE$ the bisector of $\angle B$. Prove that $AD,CF,BE$ are concurrent if and only if $\cos\gamma\tan\beta=\sin\alpha$.

Eight guests arrive at a hotel with four rooms, and no room may be empty. Each guest has at most three other guests with whom they refuse to share a room. Refusal is mutual. Prove that the guests can be placed, two per room, so that everyone is satisfied.
In a triangle, the circumradius $R$ and inradius $r$ satisfy $R=2r$. Prove that the triangle is equilateral.
Given $|x|,|y|,|z|\ge2$, find the smallest possible value of $|xyz+2(x+y+z)|$.
Find all positive integer solutions $(a,b,c)$ of $$a^2=4(b+c),\qquad a^3-2b^3-4c^3=\frac12abc.$$

A function $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, where $\mathbb N$ denotes the positive integers, satisfies $f(1)=1$, $f(2n)=f(n)$ and $f(2n+1)=f(2n)+1$ for every positive integer $n$. (a) Find $M=\max_{1\le n\le1995}f(n)$. (b) Find all $n$ in this range with $f(n)=M$.
Find all real solutions of $x^2+y^2=6z$, $y^2+z^2=6x$, $z^2+x^2=6y$.

A two-pan balance is available, and weights may be placed on either pan. (a) Give four integer weights with which every integer weight from $1$ to $40$ grams can be measured. (b) Do four weights exist with which every integer weight from $1$ to $50$ grams can be measured?
Let $n?$ denote the product of all primes smaller than $n$. Prove that $n?>n$ for every positive integer $n>3$.

Let $f:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ be continuous and strictly increasing, with $f(0)=0$, $f(1)=1$, and let $g=f^{-1}$. Prove that $$\sum_{k=1}^{9}f\left(\frac{k}{10}\right)+\sum_{k=1}^{9}g\left(\frac{k}{10}\right)\le\frac{99}{10}.$$
Let $n\ge12$ and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be pairwise coprime positive integers, all smaller than $9n^2$. Prove that at least one of them is prime.

In a country, every two cities are joined by either a road or a railway, but not both. Prove that one can choose a single type of transport so that every city can be reached from every other city by that type of transport, passing through at most two intermediate cities.

A square of side $10^6$ has a corner square of side $10^{-3}$ removed. The remaining region is partitioned into $10$ rectangles. Prove that at least one rectangle has the ratio of its longer side to its shorter side at least $9:1$.

Two circles of equal radius are internally tangent to a larger circle at $A$ and $B$. Let $M$ lie on the larger circle, and let $A',B'$ be the second intersections of $MA,MB$ with the corresponding smaller circles. Prove that $AB\parallel A'B'$.

Segments $[A_i,B_i]$, $i=1,\ldots,n$, lie in a plane and do not pass through a point $O$. Suppose $\sum_{i=1}^n\angle A_iOB_i<180^\circ$, where each angle is the smaller angle. Prove that there is a line through $O$ which intersects none of the segments.
Prove that some positive multiple of $2^{1998}$ has a decimal representation using only the digits $1$ and $2$.

Coins are placed on a square-cell board, with at most one coin per cell. A configuration is called boring if four coins occupy the vertices of a rectangle with sides parallel to the board's sides. (a) Prove that every configuration with more than $3mn/4$ coins on an $m\times n$ board is boring. (b) Prove that every configuration of $26$ coins on a $7\times7$ board is boring.

A person has a seven-branched candelabrum and identical candles. On the first evening, they light one candle and extinguish it after one hour. On the second evening, they light two candles and extinguish them after exactly one hour. Continuing in this way, they light seven candles on the seventh evening; after one hour all candles are exactly consumed, so no extinguishing is needed. How did they choose the candles to light each evening?
(a) Find real numbers $a,b$ such that $|ax+b-\sqrt{x}|\le1/24$ for every $x\in[1,4]$. (b) Prove that $1/24$ cannot be replaced by a smaller positive number.
A polygonal line of length $1001$ is drawn in a unit square. Prove that some line parallel to a side of the square meets the polygonal line at at least $500$ points.
A convex polygon $M$ contains no triangle of area greater than $1$. Prove that $M$ can be contained in a triangle of area at most $4$.
A cubic polynomial $P(x)=ax^3+\cdots$ satisfies $|P(x)|<1$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$. Prove that $|a|<30$. Is it always true that $|a|<9/2$?
There are $1999$ insects in cells of a $2000\times2000$ board, with no two in cells sharing a side. Prove that one insect can move to an adjacent cell so that it still has no neighbour.
An integer-coefficient polynomial $P$ satisfies $P(a)=1$, $P(b)=2$, $P(c)=3$ for integers $a,b,c$. Prove that $b$ lies between $a$ and $c$.
There are $n$ unit vectors in a plane whose sum is zero. Prove that they can be ordered so that the length of the sum of the first $k$ vectors is at most $2$ for every $2\le k\le n-1$.
Prove that $2^{2^n}-1$ has at least $n$ distinct prime divisors for every positive integer $n$.
What is the greatest number of points that can be placed in a disk of radius $1$ so that the distance between every two is greater than $\sqrt2$?

A rectangular $2m\times2n$ grid of points is coloured blue and red so that each row has $m$ blue and $m$ red points, and each column has $n$ blue and $n$ red points. Every segment joining two adjacent points of the same colour, in one row or column, is coloured that colour. Prove that the number of blue segments equals the number of red segments.
A convex quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. Perpendiculars are drawn from the intersection of its diagonals to its four sides. Prove that their feet form a quadrilateral with an incircle.
Prove that for every integer $n\ge0$, the equation $$\frac{x^{2000}}{2001^n}+\frac{x^{1999}}{2000^n}+\cdots+\frac{x^2}{3^n}+\frac{x}{2^n}+1=0$$ has no real solutions.

Every point of the plane is coloured black or white. Prove that there exist (a) three points of the same colour, one of which is the midpoint of the segment joining the other two; (b) three points of the same colour forming an equilateral triangle.

Avi hides a coin at a distance of at most $N$ metres from Benny. Benny may move in any direction in the plane, each step having length at most $1$ metre. After each step, Avi tells him whether he has moved closer to or farther from the coin. Describe a strategy that brings Benny within $1$ metre of the coin in at most $8+3N/2$ steps.
Points $P,Q,R$ lie on the sides of triangle $ABC$, with $AP:PB=BQ:QC=CR:RA=2:1$. Triangle $PQR$ has the same angles as $ABC$, in the corresponding order. Prove that $ABC$ is equilateral.
Prove that $2^p+3^p$ is not a perfect square for any prime $p$.
Positive real numbers $a<b<c$ and $p<q<r$ satisfy $a+b+c=p+q+r$ and $abc=pqr$. Suppose also that $p,q,r\in[a,c]$. Prove that $a=p$, $b=q$, $c=r$.
For which positive integers $n$ are $n+1$, $n+11$ and $n+111$ all prime?

A function $f$ on $[0,1]$ satisfies $f((x+y)/2)\le f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x,y\in[0,1]$, and $f(0)=f(1)=0$. (a) Prove that $f(x)\ge0$ for all $x$. (b) Prove that $f$ has infinitely many zeros in $[0,1]$. (c) Prove that if $f(x)\le A$ on $[0,1/2]$ for some constant $A$, then $f(x)\le A$ on $[0,1]$. (d) Prove that if $f(x)\le2002(1-x)$ on $[0,1]$, then $f$ is identically zero. (e) Construct a function satisfying the two original conditions that is not identically zero.
Six open disks (their boundary circles are excluded) lie in a plane; three are blue and three red. Every blue disk intersects every red disk. Prove that two disks of the same colour intersect.

An integer sequence begins with $x_0=1$, $x_1=0$, $x_2=2$ and satisfies $x_{n+2}=2x_n+x_{n-1}$ for $n\ge1$. Prove that for every positive integer $m$, the sequence contains two consecutive terms both divisible by $m$.
An infinite table contains real numbers between $0$ and $2002$. Each entry is the average of its four neighbours, two in its row and two in its column. Prove that all entries are equal.
In a certain calendar year, the numbers of Sundays and Tuesdays are equal. Must the number of Mondays also equal this number?
A school has several pupils. Each pupil hits at least one other pupil. Prove that the headmaster can divide the pupils into three classes so that no two pupils in the same class hit one another.
A point $P$ inside a parallelogram $ABCD$ satisfies $\angle ADP=\angle ABP$. Prove that $\angle BAP=\angle BCP$.

A teacher asks for representations of $987654321$ as a sum of two positive integers, each using all digits $1,2,\ldots,9$ exactly once. Alex gives $396$ different representations, treating $A+B$ and $B+A$ as the same, and claims to have found them all. Prove that he is wrong.
(a) Find a function $f$, together with its domain, such that $f(f(x))=x^2-2$ for every $x\in[1/2,2]$. (b) Prove that this is impossible if the identity is required for every $x\in[-2,2]$.
How many positive integers divisible by $8$ can be formed using the digits $4,5,6,7,8,9$ exactly once each, with no two adjacent digits of the same parity?
Triangle $ABC$ has altitudes $h_a=2$, $h_b=4$, $h_c=y$ from $A,B,C$, respectively. How many such triangles exist when (a) $y=1$; (b) $y=3$?
Real numbers satisfy $(a+b+c)(x+y+z)=3$ and $(a^2+b^2+c^2)(x^2+y^2+z^2)=4$. Prove that $ax+by+cz\ge0$.

At every lattice point $(m,n)$ with positive integer coordinates, a positive integer $f(m,n)$ is written. Each positive integer occurs fewer than $2006$ times in the entire plane. Prove that there exist positive integers $m,n$ with $f(m,n)>mn$.

In Laputa there are $20$ cities, with a road joining every pair. A collection of roads is called a cycle if it can be traversed starting and ending at the same city and using each of its roads exactly once. The law allows one road to be deleted from any cycle of four roads. Can a sequence of legal deletions leave only a cycle of length $20$? If so, explain how; otherwise, prove it is impossible.
Write $(3^{44}-1)/80$ as $m_1^4+\cdots+m_k^4$, where the $m_i$ are integers, using as few summands as possible.
Is every positive integer whose decimal digit sum is $2007$ divisible by $2007$?
For positive real numbers $a,b,c$, find all possible values of $$\arccos\frac{a}{\sqrt{a+b}\sqrt{a+c}}+\arccos\frac{b}{\sqrt{b+a}\sqrt{b+c}}+\arccos\frac{c}{\sqrt{c+a}\sqrt{c+b}}.$$
Points $A,B,C,D,E$ lie on a circle, and chords $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at $F$. Suppose $AE=CE=FE$. Prove that $BD\perp EF$.

Jack leads a band of $40$ pirates, whose ranks are $151,152,\ldots,190$. They sit around a circle, and each pirate receives a sum equal to the absolute difference between the ranks of their two neighbours. Arrange them so that the total payment is as large as possible, and give an example attaining it.
Let $A$ be a set of $60$ points in a plane, and let $B$ be the set of distinct distances between pairs of distinct points of $A$. Show that $|B|$ can be (a) smaller than $50$; (b) smaller than $25$.

The Green Man drives from home to work at a constant $70$ km/h and stops only at traffic lights. Each light alternates between green and red, spending the same fixed number of minutes in each colour; different lights may have different periods. He always stops at red lights and never at green lights. His travel time depends only on his departure time. Suppose the set of possible travel times includes $30$ and $32$ minutes. Must some departure time give a journey of exactly $31$ minutes?
Find all pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$ for which the sum of $a+b$, $|a-b|$, $ab$ and $a/b$ equals $2008$.

Given a triangle $ABC$, construct $A_1,B_1,C_1$ so that $B$ is the midpoint of $A_1C$, $A$ is the midpoint of $C_1B$, and $C$ is the midpoint of $B_1A$. (a) Find the ratio of the area of $ABC$ to that of $A_1B_1C_1$. (b) If only $A_1,B_1,C_1$ remain, explain how to reconstruct $A,B,C$ with ruler and compass.

A function $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfies $f(1)=1$, $f(2)=2$ and, for every positive integer $n$, $$f(3n)=5f(n),\quad f(3n+1)=f(3n)+1,\quad f(3n+2)=f(3n)+2.$$ (a) For how many positive integers $n$ is $f(n)<1000$? (b) For how many of these $n$ is $f(n)$ even?

An enchanted palace has $120$ rooms arranged in a circle and numbered clockwise. Each room contains either a princess or a dragon; initially there are $K$ princesses and $120-K$ dragons. At the main gate is a bag containing stones numbered $1$ to $120$. One hundred and twenty princes arrive, not necessarily simultaneously. Each draws a stone without replacement and goes directly to the indicated room. On finding a dragon, a prince defeats it, turning it into a princess, then continues clockwise to the next room. On finding a princess, he kisses her, turning her into a dragon that immediately eats him. Several princes may be in the palace at once, but no two may be in the same room simultaneously. What is the final outcome for the princes and the creatures in the rooms? Justify your answer.
What is the greatest possible length of an open interval such that every monic polynomial of degree $2008$ whose other coefficients all lie in that interval has no real roots?

Twelve parties participate in parliamentary elections. A party with less than $5\%$ of the votes receives no seats. The $120$ seats are distributed among the remaining parties in proportion to their vote totals. What is the largest number of seats a party receiving exactly $25\%$ of the votes can obtain?
In triangle $ABC$, points $A',B',C'$ lie on $BC,AC,AB$, respectively, so that $AA'$ is an altitude, $BB'$ a median, and $CC'$ an angle bisector. If $A'B'C'$ is equilateral, must $ABC$ be equilateral?
What is the smallest digit sum of a positive integer divisible by $34$?
Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which $n,n+1,n+2$ are all squarefree, that is, none is divisible by the square of an integer greater than $1$.
Each pair among $2009$ points in a plane is more than $1$ unit apart. Prove that $287$ of the points can be chosen so that every pair among them is more than $\sqrt3$ units apart.

A game board consists of cells with integer coordinates $(x,y)$ in the first quadrant, $x,y\ge0$. Initially each cell with $x+y\le n$ contains one soldier. Two kinds of moves are allowed: replace two soldiers in opposite neighbouring cells $(x-1,y),(x+1,y)$ or $(x,y-1),(x,y+1)$ by one soldier in the interior cell $(x,y)$; or replace one soldier in a neighbouring cell by one soldier in a boundary cell, where $x=0$ or $y=0$. How many soldiers can be present simultaneously on the diagonal $x+y=n+1$ during the game?

Harry Potter reaches a confectioner's shop in Hogsmeade. His money buys exactly $12$ magic sweets and $15$ chocolate frogs, or exactly $10$ chocolate frogs and $30$ peppermint kisses, or exactly $45$ peppermint kisses and $18$ magic sweets. What is the greatest number of magic sweets he can buy?
(a) Can $2010$ be expressed as a sum of two or more consecutive odd integers? Give an example or explain why not. (b) Find all such representations of $2009$.

Seven players enter a round-robin tennis tournament in which every pair plays once and there are no draws. For each player, a list is formed as follows: the first list contains only that player; the second contains that player and everyone they defeated; each subsequent list contains the preceding list and everyone defeated by any player on that list. The players enter their results into a computer, which reveals that, for one player, the seventh list differs from the sixth. How many matches have been played so far?
Find all polynomials $p(x)=ax^2+bx+c$ with rational coefficients such that $p(x)$ is irrational for every irrational $x$.
Describe the locus of the centroids of all acute triangles inscribed in a given circle. The centroid is the intersection of the medians.

Danny wants to open a safe whose lock is an $n\times n$ table containing a digit from $0$ to $9$ in every row and column position. There is a button for each row and each column. Pressing a row button increases all digits in that row by $1$, modulo $10$; pressing a column button decreases all digits in that column by $1$, modulo $10$. Opening the safe requires making every entry $0$. Danny remembers that some sequence of button presses opens it. Prove that he can do so in (a) fewer than $18n$ presses; (b) at most $9n$ presses, where the table is $n\times n$.
We are given $5771$ weights weighing $1,2,3,\ldots,5770,5771$. We partition the weights into $n$ sets of equal weight. What is the maximal $n$ for which this is possible?
Evaluate the sum $$\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{1\cdot3}}+\sqrt{2-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{3\cdot5}}+\sqrt{3-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{5\cdot7}}+\cdots+\sqrt{40-\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{79\cdot81}}.$$

In the government of some foreign country there are $12$ ministers. Each minister has $5$ friends and $6$ enemies in the government (friendship and enmity are symmetric relations). A triple of ministers is called uniform if all three of them are friends with each other, or all three of them are enemies of each other. How many uniform triples are there?

Let $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3$ be three congruent circles that are tangent to each other. A circle $\beta$ is tangent to them at the points $A_1,A_2,A_3$, respectively. Let $P$ be a point on $\beta$ different from $A_1,A_2,A_3$. For $i=1,2,3$, let $B_i$ be the second intersection point of the line $PA_i$ with the circle $\alpha_i$. Prove that triangle $B_1B_2B_3$ is equilateral.

We have two lists of numbers: one initially contains $1,6,11,\ldots,96$, and the other initially contains $4,9,14,\ldots,99$. In every turn, we erase two numbers from one of the lists and write $\frac{1}{3}$ of their sum (not necessarily an integer) in the other list. We continue this process until no move is possible.

(a) Prove that at the end of the process there is exactly one number in each list.

(b) Prove that these two numbers are not equal.

There are $N$ red cards and $N$ blue cards. Each card has a positive integer between $1$ and $N$ (inclusive) written on it. Prove that we can choose a nonempty subset of the red cards and a nonempty subset of the blue cards such that the sum of the numbers on the chosen red cards equals the sum of the numbers on the chosen blue cards.

The circles shown in the figure are tangent to one another and to the sides of the rectangle. The radius of the largest circle is $1$. Find the area of the rectangle.

In a certain country, seven guards take turns guarding an object continuously. Each guard works for seven consecutive hours every day, at fixed times. Prove that one guard can be dismissed so that the remaining six can still guard the object continuously, without changing any remaining guard's working hours.
Real numbers $a,b,c$ satisfy $a^3(b+c)+b^3(a+c)+c^3(a+b)=0$. Prove that $ab+bc+ca\le 0$.

In each cell of a $7\times7$ board, choose one diagonal and colour one of the two resulting triangles black. What is the largest possible area of a connected black region? Regions are considered connected when they are joined along sides.
Find all integer solutions $(a,b)$ of $a^3+3ab^2+7b^3=2011$.

Points $O,A,B,C$ lie in a plane so that $\angle AOB$, $\angle BOC$ and $\angle COA$ are obtuse. Choose points $X,Y,Z$ on $OA,OB,OC$, respectively, with $OX=OY=OZ$, and points $K,L,M$ on $OX,OY,OZ$, respectively. Lines $AL$ and $BK$ intersect at $R
otin XY$; segment $XY$ meets $BK$ and $AL$ at $R_1$ and $R_2$, respectively. Lines $CL$ and $BM$ intersect at $P
otin YZ$; segment $YZ$ meets $BM$ and $CL$ at $P_1$ and $P_2$, respectively. Lines $CK$ and $AM$ intersect at $Q
otin XZ$; segment $XZ$ meets $AM$ and $CK$ at $Q_1$ and $Q_2$, respectively. Prove that if $PP_1=PP_2$ and $QQ_1=QQ_2$, then $RR_1=RR_2$.

Six coins, each of radius $1$ cm, are arranged as in the figure. The first is tangent to the second, the second to the third, the third to the fourth, the fourth to the fifth, the fifth to the sixth, and the sixth to the first. No other pair is tangent. The empty region between the coins has a curved, star-like boundary. What is the perimeter of this boundary?

Let $A=\{1,2,\ldots,2012\}$. A subset $B\subseteq A$ is called reduced if, for any $x,y\in B$ (not necessarily distinct), $xy\notin B$. For example, a subset containing $3,5,15$ is not reduced, nor is one containing $4,16$. (a) Find the largest possible size of a reduced subset of $A$. (b) Find the number of reduced subsets having this largest size.
Let $p(x)=x^4-5773x^3-46464x^2-5773x+46$. Find the sum of the arctangents of all its real roots.
How many positive integers smaller than $1000000$ are divisible by $7$ and use only the digits $0,1,9$ in their decimal representation?

An integer point in the plane is a point whose Cartesian coordinates are both integers. A triangle has integer vertices and no other integer points on its sides. Exactly four integer points lie strictly inside the triangle. Must these four points be collinear?

Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be positive real numbers with $x_1+\cdots+x_n=n$. Prove that $$\frac{x_1}{x_2}+\frac{x_2}{x_3}+\cdots+\frac{x_{n-1}}{x_n}+\frac{x_n}{x_1}\le\frac{4}{x_1x_2\cdots x_n}+n-4.$$

Consider the number $$\left(101^2-100^2\right)\cdot\left(102^2-101^2\right)\cdot\left(103^2-102^2\right)\cdots\left(200^2-199^2\right).$$ (a) Determine its units digit.

(b) Determine its tens digit.

Let $A_1A_2A_3$, $B_1B_2B_3$, $C_1C_2C_3$ be three equilateral triangles, the vertices of each triangle numbered clockwise. It is given that $A_3=B_3=C_3$. Let $M$ be the centroid of triangle $A_1B_1C_1$ and $N$ the centroid of triangle $A_2B_2C_2$. Prove that triangle $A_3MN$ is equilateral.

Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex hexagon. Inside the hexagon there is a point $K$ such that $ABCK$ and $DEFK$ are both parallelograms. Prove that the three lines joining $A,B,C$ to the midpoints of the segments $CE,DF,EA$, respectively, meet at one point.

We are given a row of $n\geq7$ tiles. On each of the leftmost $3$ tiles there is a white piece, and on each of the rightmost $3$ tiles there is a black piece. White and Black play in turns, White starting. In each move a player takes a piece of his color and moves it to an adjacent tile, provided that tile is not occupied by a piece of the same color. If the new tile is empty, nothing happens. If it is occupied by a piece of the opposite color, both pieces are destroyed. The player who destroys the last two pieces wins the game. Which player has a winning strategy, and what is it? (The answer may depend on $n$.)
Let $p$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients satisfying $p(16)=36$, $p(14)=16$, $p(5)=25$. Determine all possible values of $p(10)$.

Let $n\ge2$ be an integer. Find the maximal real number $k$ such that for any $n$ real numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ $$\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2+\cdots+x_n^2}\geq k\cdot\min(|x_1-x_2|,|x_2-x_3|,\ldots,|x_{n-1}-x_n|,|x_n-x_1|).$$
Find one real value of $x$ satisfying $$\frac{x^7}{7}=1+\sqrt[7]{10}\,x\left(x^2-\sqrt[7]{10}\right)^2.$$

(a) Find an example of three positive integers $a,b,c$ satisfying $31a+30b+28c=365$.

(b) Prove that any triple $a,b,c$ of positive integers satisfying this condition also satisfies $a+b+c=12$.
The altitudes of a triangle have lengths $\frac{1}{5},\frac{1}{5},\frac{1}{8}$. Evaluate the area of the triangle.
Prove that the number $$\left(\frac{76}{\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{77}-\sqrt[3]{75}}-\sqrt[3]{5775}}+\frac{1}{\frac{76}{\sqrt[3]{77}+\sqrt[3]{75}}+\sqrt[3]{5775}}\right)^3$$ is an integer.

Let $k,m,n$ be positive integers such that $n^m$ is divisible by $m^n$ and $m^k$ is divisible by $k^m$.

(a) Prove that $n^k$ is divisible by $k^n$.

(b) Find an example of $k,m,n$ satisfying these conditions, where all three numbers are distinct and greater than $1$.

Let $ABCD$ be a tetrahedron. Denote by $S_1$ its inscribed sphere, tangent to all four faces, and by $S_2$ the exscribed sphere lying outside the face $ABC$, tangent to the face $ABC$ and to the planes of the faces $ABD$, $ACD$, $BCD$. Let $K$ be the point of tangency of $S_1$ with the face $ABC$, $L$ the point of tangency of $S_2$ with the face $ABC$, and $T$ the foot of the perpendicular from $D$ to the face $ABC$. Prove that $L,T,K$ lie on one line.

Let $n\geq1$ be an integer. $n$ lamps are placed in a line. At minute $0$ some lamps are on (maybe all of them). Every minute the state of the lamps changes: a lamp is on at minute $t+1$ if and only if at minute $t$ exactly one of its neighbors is on (the two lamps at the ends have one neighbor each, all other lamps have two neighbors). For which values of $n$ can we guarantee that all lamps will be off after some time?

The Fibonacci sequence $F_n$ is defined by $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$ and $F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}$ for all integers $n\geq2$. Let $p\geq3$ be a prime number.

(a) Prove that $F_{p-1}+F_{p+1}-1$ is divisible by $p$.

(b) Prove that $F_{p^{k+1}-1}+F_{p^{k+1}+1}-\left(F_{p^k-1}+F_{p^k+1}\right)$ is divisible by $p^{k+1}$ for every positive integer $k$.

Nina and Meir are walking along a $3$ km path towards grandma's house. They start walking at the same time from the same point. Meir's speed is $4$ km/h and Nina's speed is $3$ km/h. Along the path there are several benches. Whenever Nina or Meir reaches a bench, they sit on it for some time and eat a cookie. Nina always takes $t$ minutes to eat a cookie, and Meir always takes $2t$ minutes, where $t$ is a positive integer. It turns out that Nina and Meir reached grandma's house at the same time. How many benches were there? Find all options.

We are given a cone with height $6$ whose base is a circle of radius $\sqrt{2}$. Inside the cone there is an inscribed cube: its bottom face lies on the base of the cone, and all of its top vertices lie on the cone. What is the length of the edge of the cube?

Denote by $S(n)$ the sum of the digits of $n$. Given a positive integer $N$, we consider the following process: we take the sum of digits $S(N)$, then its sum of digits $S(S(N))$, then $S(S(S(N)))$, and so on, until we are left with a one-digit number. The number of times we have to apply $S(\cdot)$ is called the depth of $N$. For example, the depth of $49$ is $2$, since $S(49)=13$ and $S(13)=4$, and the depth of $45$ is $1$, since $S(45)=9$.

(a) Prove that every positive integer $N$ has a finite depth.

(b) Let $x(n)$ be the minimal positive integer with depth $n$. Find the residue of $x(5776)$ modulo $6$.

(c) Find the residue of $x(5776)-x(5708)$ modulo $2016$.

The Fibonacci sequence $F_n$ is defined by $F_1=F_2=1$ and $F_n=F_{n-1}+F_{n-2}$ for all integers $n\geq3$. Let $m,n\geq1$ be integers. Find the minimal degree $d$ for which there exists a polynomial $f(x)=a_dx^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+a_1x+a_0$ satisfying $f(k)=F_{m+k}$ for all $k=0,1,\ldots,n$.

Points $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_{12}$ are the vertices of a regular $12$-gon, in this order. The $12$ diagonals $A_1A_6,A_2A_7,A_3A_8,\ldots,A_{11}A_4,A_{12}A_5$ are marked. Let $X$ be a point of the plane, and let $B_1,B_2,\ldots,B_{12}$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $X$ to the lines containing the marked diagonals, so that $B_1$ lies on the line $A_1A_6$, $B_2$ on the line $A_2A_7$, and so on. Evaluate the ratio $$\frac{XA_1+XA_2+\cdots+XA_{12}}{B_1B_6+B_2B_7+\cdots+B_{12}B_5}.$$

Let $P(n)$ be the product of the decimal digits of $n$; for example, $P(1948)=1\cdot9\cdot4\cdot8=288$. (a) Calculate $P(1)+P(2)+\cdots+P(2016)$. (b) Find the largest value of $P(n)/n$ for $2016\le n\le5777$.

A large supply of congruent right triangles is available; each has side lengths $3,4,5$. What is the greatest number of these triangles that can be placed inside a $20\times20$ square without overlapping?
Rational numbers $p,q,x$ satisfy $p^2-xq^2=1$, and $(x,p)\ne(0,-1)$. Prove that there exist integers $a,b$ such that $$p=\frac{a^2+xb^2}{a^2-xb^2},\qquad q=\frac{2ab}{a^2-xb^2}.$$
Let $ABCDE$ be a regular pentagon, and let $X$ lie on its circumcircle on the minor arc $AE$. Prove that $|AX|+|CX|+|EX|=|BX|+|DX|$.

Let $f:\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q\to\mathbb Q$ satisfy $$f\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2},\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right)\le\frac{f(x_1,y_1)+f(x_2,y_2)}2$$ for all rational $x_1,x_2,y_1,y_2$, and suppose that $f(0,0)<0$ and $f(x,y)>1$ whenever $x^2+y^2>100$. Prove that there is a positive rational number $b$ such that, for all rational $x,y$, $$f(x,y)\ge b\sqrt{x^2+y^2}-\frac1b.$$

An $m\times n$ table contains integers. Rehoboam and Asher play a game. On each turn, Rehoboam may first interchange two columns. He then chooses some rows and appends a new row whose entries are the sums of the corresponding entries in his chosen rows. Asher chooses one of those rows and deletes it, so the table again has $m$ rows. Prove that Rehoboam has a strategy ensuring that, after finitely many turns, no entry is smaller than the entry immediately to its right, regardless of Asher's choices.

$n$ people sit in a circle. Each of them is either a liar (always lies) or a truth-teller (always tells the truth), and everybody knows who is who. In turn, each person says: "the person two seats to my left is a truth-teller". It is known that there is at least one liar and at least one truth-teller in the circle.

(a) Is it possible that $n=2017$?

(b) Is it possible that $n=5778$?

An arithmetic progression is an infinite sequence $a_n=a_0+nd$ for $n=1,2,\ldots$, where $a_0,d$ are constants. A geometric progression is an infinite sequence $b_n=b_0q^n$ for $n=1,2,\ldots$, where $b_0,q$ are constants. (a) Does every arithmetic progression of integers contain an infinite subsequence that is a geometric progression? (b) Does every arithmetic progression of real numbers contain such an infinite subsequence?
Determine the minimal and the maximal values of the expression $$\frac{|a+b|+|b+c|+|c+a|}{|a|+|b|+|c|},$$ where $a,b,c$ are real numbers, not all zero.

The three-digit number $999$ has a special property: it is divisible by $27$, and its digit sum is also divisible by $27$. The four-digit number $5778$ also has this property, since it is divisible by $27$ and its digit sum is divisible by $27$. How many four-digit numbers have this property?

The sequence $a_n$ is defined for $n\geq 10$ by the following rules:

• $a_{10}=5778$;

• if $a_n=0$, then $a_{n+1}=0$;

• if $a_n\neq0$, then $a_{n+1}$ is the number whose base-$(n+1)$ representation equals the base-$n$ representation of the number $a_n -1$.

For example, $a_{11}=5\cdot11^3+7\cdot11^2+7\cdot11+7=7586$ and $a_{12}=5\cdot12^3+7\cdot12^2+7\cdot12+6=9738$.

(a) Does there exist $n\geq10$ with $a_n=0$?

(b) Is $a_{1\,000\,000}=0$?

(c) Is $a_{100^{100^{100}}}=0$?

A uniform covering of the integers $1,2,\ldots,n$ is a finite multiset of subsets of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ such that each number lies in the same number of sets of the covering. A covering may contain the same subset several times, it must contain at least one subset, and it may contain the empty set. For example, $(\{1\},\{1\},\{2,3\},\{3,4\},\{2,4\})$ is a uniform covering of $1,2,3,4$ (every number occurs in two sets), and the covering consisting only of the empty set is also uniform (every number occurs in zero sets).

Given two uniform coverings, their sum (denoted by $\oplus$) is the uniform covering obtained by taking the sets of both coverings together. For example, $$(\{1\},\{1\},\{2,3\},\{3,4\},\{2,4\})\oplus(\{1\},\{2\},\{3\},\{4\})=(\{1\},\{1\},\{1\},\{2\},\{3\},\{4\},\{2,3\},\{3,4\},\{2,4\}).$$ A uniform covering is called non-composite if it is not the sum of two uniform coverings. Prove that for every $n\geq1$ there are only finitely many non-composite uniform coverings of $1,2,\ldots,n$.

A kindergarten has three clubs: judo, agriculture and mathematics. Each child belongs to exactly one club, and every club has at least one child. There are $32$ children. When the teacher asked six children to tidy the classroom, she discovered that exactly half the judo club, a quarter of the agriculture club and an eighth of the mathematics club had volunteered. How many children belong to each club?

The number $1$ is written on a board $9999$ times. The following operations are allowed: erase four numbers of the form $x,x,y,y$ and replace them by $x-y,x+y$; or erase any occurrence of $0$. Guy receives $17$ cards, each bearing an integer; the integers need not be positive or distinct. For every card, the square of its number equals the sum of the numbers on the other cards. Determine every possible collection of cards: which numbers occur, and how many times each occurs.

A set of integers is called wonderful if every integer can be obtained from its elements by finitely many operations of the following kind: whenever $x,y$ belong to the set, adjoin $xy-y^2-y+x$. Prove that every wonderful set contains at least $8$ elements.

In a plane, three blue points $A,B,C$ are noncollinear, and two red points $P,Q$ are marked; no three of the five marked points are collinear, and no four are concyclic. A circle is separating if it contains all three points of one colour strictly inside it and all points of the other colour strictly outside it. Seven coins look identical; four are genuine and three are counterfeit. All genuine coins have equal weight, and all counterfeit coins have equal weight. A counterfeit coin is lighter than a genuine one. In one weighing, two groups of coins may be compared on a balance. What is the smallest number of weighings needed to identify at least one counterfeit coin?

A mathematics conference has $202$ participants from Israel, Greece and Japan. On the first day, every pair from the same country shakes hands. On the second day, every pair with exactly one Israeli shakes hands. On the third day, every pair consisting of an Israeli and a Greek shakes hands. Altogether there are $20200$ handshakes. How many participants are Israeli?
